pages.text: Cambodia's Premier University Royal University of Phnom Penh Since 1960, we've been shaping Cambodia's future leaders. Join our community of 20,000+ students pursuing excellence in education, research, and innovation. Explore Programs News & Scholarships Premier Science Facility STEM Research & Innovation Building modern multi-story facility designed to foster scientific discovery and advanced technical training for the digital age. Explore Programs News & Scholarships IFL Building This building is the Main Building of the Institute of Foreign Languages (IFL) Designed by the legendary Cambodian architect Vann Molyvann and completed in 1972, this building is a masterpiece of New Khmer Architecture. Explore Programs News & Scholarships Campus 1 Icon The IISPP International Hall A signature architectural landmark at Campus 1, symbolizing the gateway to international exchange and global education. Explore Programs News & Scholarships A Sanctuary for Learning Nature Meets Knowledge Beyond the lecture halls, our campus provides a tranquil environment designed to inspire reflection, creativity, and a balanced student life. Explore Programs News & Scholarships H.E. Prof. Chet Chealy Rector of RUPP H.E. Prof. Chet Chealy Rector of RUPP Welcome to RUPP Message From The Rector Welcome to RUPP Message From The Rector "The stands as Cambodia’s oldest and largest public university, widely recognized as the flagship institution for higher education in the nation." At the core of RUPP’s mission is Teaching and Learning. The university offers high-quality education across a diverse array of disciplines, equipping graduates to be both academically proficient and socially responsible. Its programs prioritize critical thinking, problem-solving, and adaptability—skills that are vital for navigating the challenges of a rapidly evolving society. By fostering these attributes, RUPP guarantees that its graduates are not only employable but also capable of making meaningful contributions to the development of Cambodia. Research and Innovation constitute the second pillar of RUPP’s mission. As a center for intellectual exploration, the university promotes research that tackles national challenges while also contributing to global knowledge. Its initiatives cover a wide range of fields, from environmental studies to technological advancements, with the goal of producing solutions that are relevant locally yet significant on an international scale. This dual focus enhances Cambodia’s ability to address urgent issues while establishing RUPP as a participant in global academic discussions. Social Engagement rounds out the triad of RUPP’s mission. The university actively collaborates with communities to promote equity, sustainability, and the preservation of culture. Through outreach initiatives, partnerships, and service-learning opportunities, RUPP fortifies the connection between academia and society. This dedication ensures that education transcends the confines of the classroom, extending into communities and reinforcing the role of higher education as a catalyst for social advancement. RUPP works closely with the Royal Government and industries to align its academic and research priorities with national development strategies. This cooperation ensures that graduates are equipped with practical skills and that research supports Cambodia’s socio-economic growth. By tailoring curricula to labor market needs, RUPP enhances employability and ensures relevance in a rapidly evolving economy. This model strengthens the link between education and national development, making RUPP a key partner in Cambodia’s progress. Equally significant is RUPP’s dedication to internationalization. The university actively engages on a global scale by forming partnerships with universities and research institutions around the world. Internationalization enhances teaching and research through faculty exchanges, collaborative projects, and scholarship opportunities. It also provides students with exposure to a variety of perspectives, equipping them to succeed in a globalized economy while aiding Cambodia’s integration into the ASEAN and international academic communities. This global perspective bolsters RUPP’s academic excellence and empowers students to emerge as leaders in both local and international contexts. Ethical Conduct & Responsibility Commit to fulfilling the actions and responsibilities of a professional and well-rounded citizen. Educational Philosophy has an educational philosophy for teaching and learning that aims to develop human capital resources with critical reasoning and ethical decision-making skills, research and innovative skills, well-rounded citizenship in diverse cultural settings, awareness of the potential needs of society and the region, and able students to the workforce or to create jobs and develop themselves to be professionals, contributing in the advancement of nation’s prosperity, preserving Cambodian cultural and natural heritage. pages.text: Faculty of Engineering Faculty of Engineering Faculty of Engineering Introductions Contact Us Departments Environmental Engineering Information Technology Engineering Telecommunication and Electronic Engineering Bio-Engineering Automation & Supply Chain Systems Engineering Introductions Vision To pursue an excellence in teaching, research and community engagement in Engineering Education to address the challenges of ever-changing society and globalization. Mission Deliver Comprehensive and Dynamic Education : Covers core engineering principles, advanced topics, and interdisciplinary studies to build a solid foundation of knowledge and skills. Foster advancement in research : Promotes Innovation, collaboration and ethical practices; and to encourage faculty and students to think outside the box by integrating project-based learning, creative thinking methodologies, and opportunities to tackle real-world challenges; and Facilitates access to research projects, internships, and industry collaboration to give practical experience and exposure to cutting-edge technologies and practices. Cultivate a Global Perspective : Prepare students for the global engineering landscape by offering international exchange programs and fostering collaborations with global institutions. Enhance Soft Skills : Develop students' communication, teamwork, leadership, and problem-solving abilities through group projects, presentations, and leadership roles within student organizations. Encourage Lifelong Learning : Promote continuous education and professional development by encouraging students to stay abreast of emerging technologies, trends, and best practices in engineering. Engage with the Community : Involve students in community service and outreach programs to help them understand the societal impact of their work and develop a sense of social responsibility. Our Faculty offers three main skills for market demand Hard Skill Soft Skill English Faculty of Telecommunication & Electronic Engineering Faculty of Information Technology Engineering Bio-Engineering Communication Team Work Problem Solving Innovation and Creativity Study Time 4 hour / 1 week for 3 years Certification of completion DEAN'S MESSAGE DR. NGUONPHAN PHEAKDEY Dean, Faculty of Engineering On behalf of all our faculty, staff and students, welcome to the Faculty of Engineering! The Faculty of Engineering, Royal University of Phnom Penh was set up on May, 07 2013 to respond to the increase demand of the industries and private sectors in the country for qualified engineers. The faculty, with four departments, offers now seven degrees programs. We thrive to bring international experiences and new innovative engineering education such as Conceive, Design, Implement, Operate (CDIO) framework to enhance existing programs and building new programs toward international level. We ventured into offering international programs in Food technology & Engineering, Data science & Engineering, 2+2 international program in Automation and Supply Chain System Engineering, and Environmental Engineering. Our engineering programs prepare our students equipped with positive mental attitude, intellectual, entrepreneurship and leadership capacity necessary to meet the challenges of the ever-changing society. With dedication, enthusiasm and hard work, the faculty has been able to produce graduates who are capable of addressing the requirement of the industries and private sectors. The faculty is dedicated to pursue and excellent teaching and research culture to deliver high quality education. pages.text: Faculty of Science Faculty of Science Science Faculty of Science Welcome Message About the Faculty Our Teams Contact Us Departments Biology Chemistry Mathematics Environmental Science Physics Computer Science Welcome Message Asst. Prof. Meak Kamerane It is my great pleasure to welcome you to the Faculty of Science, Royal University of Phnom Penh. As the Dean of the Faculty, I am honored to lead a vibrant academic community dedicated to excellence in teaching, research, and service to society. The Faculty of Science currently consists of six departments: Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Environmental Science, and Computer Science. Each department is committed to providing high-quality education, developing scientific knowledge, and preparing students with the skills needed to meet the challenges of modern science and technology. In addition to our programs, the Faculty is proud to offer 1+3 international bachelor degree programs in Chemistry, Biology, and Computer Science associated with Angelo State University (located in Texas, USA), which provide students with opportunities to study in an international environment and strengthen their academic and professional competencies. These programs reflect our commitment to global collaboration and the continuous improvement of higher education. Our mission is to produce qualified graduates with strong scientific background, critical thinking ability, research capacity, and ethical responsibility. We strive to promote innovation, support sustainable development, and contribute to the advancement of science in Cambodia and beyond. On behalf of the Faculty of Science, I warmly welcome students, partners, and visitors to work with us in building a strong future through science and education. Asst. Prof. MEAK Kamerane Dean, Faculty of Science Royal University of Phnom Penh About the Faculty The Faculty is dedicated to high-quality teaching, pioneering research, and community service. Its primary goal is to produce graduates with the theoretical knowledge and practical technical skills necessary to support Cambodia’s goal of becoming an upper-middle-income country by 2030. Key Departments The Faculty of Science is organized into several core departments, each offering undergraduate and, in many cases, postgraduate degrees: Department of Biology: Offers a comprehensive B.Sc. in Biology, covering areas from molecular cloning to ecology. Department of Chemistry: Provides degrees in General Chemistry and Biochemistry, with a strong focus on analytical chemistry at the Master's level. Department of Computer Science: One of the most popular departments, focusing on software development, networking, and IT solutions. Department of Environmental Science: Specializes in environmental research, water and air quality, and sustainable resource management. Department of Mathematics: Focuses on pure and applied mathematics, preparing students for careers in education, data science, and research. Department of Physics: Offers B.Sc. and M.Sc. programs that balance theoretical physics with practical applications in daily life and technology. Vision To become a center of excellence in education, research, innovation, and community service in science and technology for sustainable development at the national and regional levels. Mission Provide students with knowledge, skills, and ethics in the field of science to meet national and regional needs. Reform the curriculum to align with social needs and global trends. Strengthen a suitable environment for quality research and innovation that responds to the industrial sector and social needs. Actively participate in providing community services in the fields of science and technology. Strategic Goals Goal 1: Enhance the quality of teaching and academic programs Goal 2: Strengthen research capacity and scientific publication Goal 3: Improve infrastructure, equipment, and technology Goal 4: Strengthen partnerships with industry, institutions, and communities Goal 5: Develop quality assurance and safety systems Our Team Asst. Prof. MEAK Kamerane Dean Asst. Prof. Meak Kamerane is the Dean of the Faculty of Science at Royal University of Phnom Penh with more than 30 years of distinguished experience in teaching, research, academic leadership, and university management. He specializes in statistics, data analysis, research methodology, applied mathematics, quantitative research, and statistical modeling. He obtained a Master of Science in Statistics from Université du Québec à Montréal and a Master of Science in Mathematics and Informatics from Daghestan State University(Russia) . He was also awarded the certification of “Doctorat 3ième Cycle” in Statistics through the Francophone academic program. His professional expertise includes statistical modeling, quantitative and qualitative data analysis, SAS and SPSS data analysis, S-Plus and R programming, simulation and modeling, and research consultancy for socio-economic studies with national and international organizations. Throughout his career, he has actively contributed to research projects in the fields of education, health, environment, business, economics, and social development. Since 2011, he has served as Dean of the Faculty of Science at RUPP, where he has played an important role in strengthening higher education, promoting scientific research, modernizing academic programs, and building research capacity in Cambodia. Prior to this position, he also served as Deputy Head of the Department of Computer Science and Vice-Dean of the Faculty of Science. As an experienced lecturer and researcher, Asst. Prof. Meak Kamerane has taught a wide range of courses in statistics, research methodology, quantitative methods, applied mathematics, and data analysis. He is also the author and co-author of publications in statistics, generalized biadditive models, and Biplots. In addition to his academic and administrative responsibilities, he has worked as a consultant for several national and international organizations on socio-economic and research-related projects. View Biography Chhim Meng Vice Dean Mr. Chhim Meng is the Vice Dean of the Faculty of Science at the Royal University of Phnom Penh (RUPP), where he leads the faculty's Administration. A specialist in Mathematics, Mr. Meng holds a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics from RUPP (1989) and later earned a Master of Business Administration (MBA) from Phnom Penh International University (2007). His academic foundation in the sciences, combined with advanced training in business administration, provides him with a unique skill set for managing the complex operations of a large academic faculty. Mr. Meng’s career is deeply rooted in the Department of Mathematics at RUPP, where he has served as a dedicated lecturer since 1990. In his current leadership role as Vice Dean, he utilizes his analytical background and administrative expertise to oversee strategic institutional workflows, ensuring the faculty remains an efficient and supportive environment for scientific excellence in Cambodia. pages.text: Cambodian Journal of Natural History | RUPP localStorage.setItem('cjnhTab', val))"> Journal Home Journal Issues CAMBODIA'S FIRST PEER-REVIEWED SCIENTIFIC JOURNAL The Cambodian Journal of Natural History (ISSN 2226–969X), Cambodia’s first peer-reviewed scientific journal, was launched in 2008 by the and Fauna & Flora. Today, the journal is co-published by the RUPP and Cambodia Wildlife Care , a non-profit organisation founded with the aim of protecting Cambodia’s wildlife and forests. Aimed at helping Cambodian scientists to share their findings and improve their writing skills, the journal is open access and addresses the critical need for information on the conservation status and management requirements of Cambodian biodiversity. All papers are peer-reviewed by leading national and international scientists and published in English. Many of the journal’s authors are early-career researchers with little experience of writing scientific papers, and our editors gently coach novice authors to develop their analysis and presentation. Young scientists are thus gaining valuable new skills and confidence to write up their work, while distinguished veterans can use the journal to ensure their findings reach a wide audience in Cambodia. Unlike many peer-reviewed journals, the CJNH does not charge reader or author fees as it relies entirely on the generosity of sponsors for publication and distribution to ensure as many people as possible have open access. The journal is published biannually in June and December each year by the Centre for Biodiversity Conservation (CBC) at the Royal University of Phnom Penh. The CBC is a non-profit making unit dedicated to training Cambodian biologists and the study and conservation of Cambodia’s biodiversity. PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF THE JOURNAL The Cambodian Journal of Natural History publishes original work by Cambodian and foreign scientists on all aspects of Cambodian natural history, including the status and ecology of species and habitats, new records, range extensions and checklists for species, landscape ecology, conservation policies and management plans, and human use of natural resources. The journal accepts original work by: Cambodian and foreign scientists on any aspect of Cambodian natural history Cambodian scientists on natural history studies in any part of the world The journal especially welcomes material that enhances understanding of conservation needs and has the potential to contribute to conservation management in Cambodia. MANUSCRIPTS ACCEPTED Full papers (2,000–7,000 words, excluding references) Short communications (300–2,000 words, excluding references) News (<300 words) The primary language of the journal is English, although authors of full papers are also encouraged to include a Khmer translation of their abstract. Manuscripts are accepted on a rolling basis each year and can be submitted by email to the editors at any time (<< Editor.CJNH@gmail.com >> or << Editor.CJNH@rupp.edu.kh >>). Before preparing a manuscript, authors should consult past issues of the journal for general style. Specific guidance on manuscript preparation and submission requirements are provided in the Instructions for Authors . Authors are encouraged to contact the editors at any time if questions arise. READERSHIP The journal’s readership includes conservation professionals, academics, government departments, non-governmental organisations, students and interested members of the public in Cambodia and overseas.
